author: NASASpaceflight
description:
Rocket Lab’s Neutron slips to 2027 as Relativity’s Terran R fires up and Stoke’s Nova moves toward testing. Who will reach orbit first—and how is Blue Origin preparing for a much higher launch cadence?

This Week in Spaceflight, we break down Neutron’s carbon fiber tank manufacturing challenges, Terran R’s second-stage hot fire, and Nova’s latest progress. Plus, Blue Origin outlines a massive Florida expansion, including a factory designed to produce 150 New Glenn 9x4 second stages per year, additional launch pads, and more landing platforms.

Also in this episode:
• NASA’s Artemis II heat shield findings and Artemis III preparations
• Potential Artemis changes ahead of NASA’s upcoming update
• India’s Gaganyaan separation test and methane engine development
• Griffin lunar lander and Astrolab FLIP rover milestones
• Perseverance’s new Mars driving record
• SpaceX launches, Starfall, and Japan’s MMX mission
• A Russian satellite’s close approaches to ICEYE-X36
